ANAT 392.title: Gross Anatomy of the Limbs and Trunk
ANAT 392.description: Lectures and laboratory sessions on the human gross and functional anatomy of the limbs and trunk. The course includes the study of predissected specimens. For credit only in the Department of Physical Therapy.

ANAT 393.title: Human Anatomy for Physical Therapy Students
ANAT 393.description: Microscopic systems anatomy and regional anatomy of the nervous system.
ANAT 393.prerequisiteText: Registration in Rehabilitation Sciences (RSPT) is required

ANAT 400.title: Human Anatomy
ANAT 400.description: A correlated course of study for medical and dental students of the structure of the human body including gross and radiological anatomy and embryology. Clinics are held in cooperation with the Departments of Medicine, Orthopaedics, Surgery and Family Practice. Both terms.

ANAT 401.title: Microscopic Human Anatomy
ANAT 401.description: A survey course for medical and dental students of the microscopic structure of the human body as studied by light and electron microscopy. Lectures and laboratory sessions. Both terms.

ANAT 425.title: Elements of Neuroanatomy
ANAT 425.description: An introduction to the structure of the human nervous system. Given only in conjunction with PHYL 425. (Open to Medical and Dental students only.)

ANAT 448.title: Directed Studies in Anatomy
ANAT 448.description: Permission of the Head and supervisor required.

ANAT 500.title: Gross Human Anatomy
ANAT 500.description: An advanced laboratory course in the structure of the human body.

ANAT 501.title: Microscopic Human Anatomy
ANAT 501.description: An advanced lecture and laboratory course in the microscopic structure of the human body.

ANAT 502.title: Microscopic Anatomy
ANAT 502.description: The microscopic anatomy of tissues and organs in man.

ANAT 504.title: Cell Structure and Function
ANAT 504.description: Seminar discussions of current topics in vertebrate cell biology.

ANAT 505.title: General Cytological Biophysics
ANAT 505.description: An examination of selected properties of the cell and underlying mechanisms based on the ultrastructure of the cell and on the physical chemistry of open systems.

ANAT 510.title: Neuroanatomy
ANAT 510.description: The gross and microscopic study of the nervous system in man.

ANAT 511.title: Fundamentals of Body Design: Basic Principles in Human Anatomy as Illustrated by the Organization of the Back and Upper Limb

ANAT 512.title: Functional Human Anatomy of Head and Neck Systems

ANAT 513.title: Functional Human Anatomy of the Respiratory, Cardiovascular and Gastrointestinal Systems of the Thorax and Abdomen

ANAT 514.title: Functional Human Anatomy of the Urogenital Systems: Pelvis and Perineum

ANAT 515.title: Functional Human Anatomy of the Musculoskeletal Systems: Back, Limbs and Joints

ANAT 516.title: Functional Human Neuroanatomy: Central Nervous System

ANAT 517.title: Functional Human Microscopic Anatomy: Basic Tissues, Organs and Systems

ANAT 527.title: Muscle Biophysics
ANAT 527.description: Selected topics in muscle contraction at an advanced level Permission of Head required.

ANAT 548.title: Directed Studies in Anatomy & Cell Biology

ANAT 550.title: Current Topics in the Morphological Sciences
ANAT 550.description: Lectures, demonstrations, discussions and student seminars on selected and current topics in cell biology and the anatomical sciences. Attendance is required of all M.Sc. and Ph.D. students in Anatomy & Cell Biology.

prerequisite.raw: Students must be registered in graduate-level studies in Anatomy & Cell Biology
